overview: The position is the Pirc with 3.Nf3 played before Nc3, the move order that rules out ...Bg4 trouble and keeps Bc4 or Be2 options open. Black normally continues 3...g6 4.Nc3 Bg7 or 3...c6 and transposes into the Classical Pirc. I am not sure what the named gambit is; it is a rare 3rd or 4th-move try that is not part of the usual play, so the tags describe the ordinary Pirc line reached.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nc3, Be2 and O-O (Classical set-up) with a broad e4/d4 centre.
Use the move order to avoid or steer Black's early ...Bg4.

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7, then undermine the centre with ...c5 or ...e5.
Keep a solid king position and counterattack on the queenside.

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 centre against Black d6, g6 and a fianchettoed Bg7.

character.notes: Ordinary Classical Pirc after 3...g6: imbalanced but not forcing.
